experiment: W4 knowledge-base access control: cross-user matrix and pre-recall filtering
basis: JUnit against a random local PostgreSQL + pgvector database built from schema_pg.sql; no model or embedding calls

regression.schemaUpgradeCheck: scripts/validate-agentic-research-p2-database.sh passed (fresh == upgraded catalog; legacy rows PUBLIC with owner; new rows PRIVATE)

phases: B READ on RESTRICTED + MANAGE on PRIVATE (ignored)
matrix.denialRule: ClientException and the mocked business service was never invoked

otherChecks.listFiltering: kb page and document search scopes for A, B, admin (6 checks)
otherChecks.identity: no login user, unknown user, deleted user, deleted kb -> no access (4 checks)
otherChecks.stop: owner allowed, other user denied, admin allowed, unknown task denied (4 cases)
otherChecks.research: creation rejects an unreadable kb with the not-found message and accepts it once PUBLIC; a queued run whose owner lost access fails KB_ACCESS_REVOKED at claim with 0 model calls (ResearchRunPostgresIT)

preRecallProof.setup: query vector e0; PRIVATE kb chunk = e0 (cosine 1.0); PUBLIC kb chunk = 0.6 e0 + 0.8 e1 (cosine 0.6)
preRecallProof.argument: TopK=1 still returns the public chunk for the other user; a post-recall filter would have spent the single slot on the private chunk and returned nothing
